_note: Teardown/breakdown data for the Showroom's exploded view. Anchors are in FITTED car space (auto-fit ~3.4 units long, grounded y=0, +X nose, +Y up, +Z left) — same frame as lib/systems.js. `materials` are GLB material-name substrings the frontend matches (first-match-wins in this part order — put specific parts before general ones); empty = not a mesh in this GLB, shown as an info callout. Non-modeled engine/drivetrain/suspension with those exact ids render the procedural stand-in; other non-modeled ids render a pure callout. The GT-R ships a real engine mesh (r35_engine) AND a real transmission mesh (material `material`, isolated last so it doesn't grab the PaletteMaterial* glass/paint). Copy grounded on data/cars/20-nissan-gtr-r35.json; anchors from frontend/scripts/model_meshes.mjs + the sibling .partmap.json.

parts.label: 3.8L VR38DETT Twin-Turbo V6
parts.summary: The hand-built heart — a 3.8-liter twin-turbo V6, each one assembled and signed by a single Takumi master.
parts.detail: VR38DETT — 3.8L twin-turbo V6, each unit hand-assembled and signed by one Takumi builder. 565 hp by 2017 and genuinely stout, good far past stock on a tune.
parts.watch: Very reliable when serviced on schedule; keep oil intervals short with any track use and use the specified 0W-40.

parts.label: 20" RAYS Forged Wheels
parts.summary: Twenty-inch forged alloys on wide, staggered performance rubber — the contact patch behind the launch.
parts.detail: Forged 20-inch wheels on staggered high-performance tires, sized to put 565 hp and the ATTESA AWD launch down.
parts.watch: Tires are exotic-car expensive and wear quickly — budget $1,500+ a set. Curb rash on the low-profile fronts.

parts.label: Brembo Monobloc Brakes
parts.summary: Big Brembo monobloc calipers on vented, drilled rotors — supercar stopping power.
parts.detail: Brembo monobloc calipers clamp large vented, drilled rotors (carbon-ceramics were offered on later cars) to haul a ~3,930 lb car down from supercar speed.
parts.watch: Rotors and pads are exotic-car expensive and wear quickly with track use.

parts.label: Interior & Driver's Cockpit
parts.summary: A 2+2 grand-tourer cabin — leather, carbon, and the R35's famous multi-function display.
parts.detail: Leather and carbon-fiber trim around the GT-R's signature configurable multi-function display (co-developed with Polyphony Digital), plus the paddle-shift wheel for the GR6 dual-clutch.
parts.watch: Leather bolster wear on hard-used cars; the early multi-function display electronics can age.

parts.label: Lighting & Electronics
parts.summary: The GT-R's signature quad-ring tail lamps and full lighting suite.
parts.detail: The unmistakable four-ring tail lamps plus the headlight and signal cluster — the R35's night-time signature.
parts.watch: Aging lighting electronics and control modules on early cars; costly to replace as a unit.

parts.label: Body, Aero & Glass
parts.summary: A steel, aluminum, and composite body — heavy at ~3,930 lbs but slippery and planted.
parts.detail: Mixed steel, aluminum, and composite construction with functional aero — the R35 is heavy but aerodynamically slick and rock-stable at speed.
parts.watch: Front-end stone chips and costly body panels; with the R35 it's running cost, not faults, that bite.

parts.label: GR6 Dual-Clutch Transaxle & ATTESA AWD
parts.summary: A rear-mounted 6-speed dual-clutch and the ATTESA AWD system — the secret to the launch and the balance.
parts.detail: GR6 6-speed dual-clutch mounted as a rear transaxle, fed by a carbon prop shaft and the ATTESA E-TS AWD system — the key to the 2.9-second launch and the near-50:50 balance.
parts.watch: The transaxle is the real cost: fluid service on schedule is non-negotiable, and hard launches wear the early (2009–2010) boxes.

parts.label: Bilstein DampTronic Suspension
parts.summary: Bilstein DampTronic adjustable dampers on a multilink layout — supercar grip with a real comfort mode.
parts.detail: Bilstein DampTronic adjustable dampers with a multilink layout give the R35 supercar body control plus a genuinely usable comfort setting. (Shown as a procedural stand-in — the suspension isn't a separate mesh in this model.)
parts.watch: Dampers and bushings are expensive, and the alignment is fussy after any suspension work.
